reviewCommentsList.body: I think better just remove this line entirely, rather than replace with a dummy amendment.

reviewCommentsList.author: a1q123456
reviewCommentsList.body: Yeah but completely removing it will make it impossible to test obsolete features in `Feature_test.cpp`. I can explore some ways to make it possible.

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body:
Noooo. I don't like this either. Here's what I would do:

1. Remove the placeholder feature entirely. There will now be no Obsolete amendments.
2. At the top of this test (`testObsolete`), grab `supportedAmendments()`. That returns a map from name to behavior.
3. Find the first amendment where the behavior is `Obsolete`. Use it's name as `featureName`.
4. If none are found, there's nothing to do, so `return`.

issues.title: Remove CryptoConditionsSuite stub amendment
issues.author: mDuo13
issues.body:
## Issue Description
The [CryptoConditionsSuite amendment](https://github.com/ripple/rippled/blob/develop/src/ripple/protocol/Feature.h#L86) is not fully implemented but it is listed in the code as an amendment that can be enabled. There should not be stub amendments in production releases, for several reasons, including:

- If later versions introduce a full version of the same amendment, earlier servers won't become properly amendment blocked despite lacking the code
- Any functionality tied to the stub amendment is likely undesirable in production. For example, it has been speculated that CryptoConditionsSuite, if it were to become enabled, might allow the creation of unfinishable conditional escrows.

We should remove CryptoConditionsSuite and its associated functionality from v1.6.0 ASAP. If we later introduce a full version of the amendment, we should ensure one of the following conditions is met:

- The new, full amendment has a different name, _or_ 
- Mainnet servers that had the stub amendment are already amendment blocked by a different amendment being enabled (e.g. a different v1.6.0+ amendment has already gained a majority. So this could only happen _after_ v1.6.0 is fully released.)
